correctness.rationale: The endpoints of the selected edges meet every edge exactly when the selection dominates; deletion connectivity is checked on all original vertices. The cut-first test is exhaustive since every disconnecting selection contains the boundary of some nonempty proper vertex set, which can be chosen to contain vertex zero. Independently of both supplied enumerators and their logs, I generated all four edge lists and exhausted subsets through sizes 6,6,7,6 with closed-line-neighborhood masks and residual floods. The nonzero ordinary counts through those levels are Heawood 42,1918 at 5,6; Möbius–Kantor 368 at 6; Pappus 36,2349 at 6,7; Desargues 5 at 6. Joint counts are zero before the claimed levels, then 98,8,27,5; the empty selection does not dominate. Every joint minimum has two components. Sorted sizes / cross-edge count / multiplicity are (1,13)/3/56, (4,10)/6/14, (6,8)/6/28 for Heawood, and (8,8)/6/8, (9,9)/7/27, (10,10)/6/5 for the other graphs. The small Heawood sides have residual degrees 1,1,1,3 and 2,2,2,2,2,2, and in these rows all deletions cross, so the claw and cycle are also induced. The isolated-vertex row deletes exactly three additional internal edges. I normalized both endpoints of every certificate edge, matched the complete independently generated minimum families, and independently checked each orbit witness as an adjacency-preserving bijection sending its representative to its target. Different size profiles are automorphism invariants, which proves the exact six orbits without assuming a group order.
residual_risks: These are four fixed labeled graphs with spanning deletion, not a claim about arbitrary cubic symmetric graphs or definitions that require the selected set to be an inclusion-minimal cut. No supplied executable code was run.

evidence: Proposition 2.2 evaluates standard families such as paths, trees, wheels and complete bipartite graphs, not these cubic incidence examples. Spiro–Adriaensen–Mattheus give ordinary edge domination results for projective planes: the exact q=2^(2h) statement does not cover q=2, and the bound for q>=101 does not apply there either.
broader_coverage.reasoning: The checked family results do not cover the four graphs at the relevant parameter and hypotheses. Bounds on ordinary domination do not enforce disconnection or classify how minima disconnect.

evidence: The original parameter comparison relates edge domination and edge connectivity to cut domination. The Heawood exact ordinary entry gives no disconnected minimizer, and ordinary minima and cut minima need not have the same size.
claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: Scalar ordinary domination and connectivity data cannot generally decide a joint optimum count or its geometry. Even a known scalar gamma_ct would not imply the component boundaries, internal deletions, or exact transitivity witnesses.

value.rationale: On natural cubic bipartite benchmark graphs the census distinguishes the extra cost of demanding disconnection from the geometry of how it is achieved. The same parameter yields balanced exact boundaries in three graphs but three distinct Heawood types, including minima that cannot be described solely by their separating boundary. Counts and orbit witnesses make the data usable for testing structural conjectures about symmetry and minimum dominating disconnecting sets.
residual_risks: Finite benchmark data do not establish an asymptotic pattern or a general algorithm.
